title: Hosted API SKU smoothing and cache prioritization workbook
content:
Executive summary:
Small concise summary: this workbook explores a SKU-smoothing approach that flexes model quantization, caching, and routing to improve hosted API unit economics across regions while preserving latency SLOs and quality. It prioritizes low-friction wins (cache + int8) and defines pilot steps for riskier levers (4-bit, dedicated tiling).

Assumptions & Inputs:
- Model families: rwd-7b, rwd-13b, rwd-70b, community-owl-30b
- Regions: us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1, ap-south1
- Baseline ppk (USD per 1k tokens) derived from infra costs, power, license amortization and overheads (sheet cell inputs).
- Latency sensitivity buckets: high (<=120ms), medium (120-300ms), low (>300ms) used to weight routing decisions.

Tab: Regional SKU Matrix (sample rows)
Columns: region | model_family | q_profile | avg_seq_len | reqs_per_min | tokens_per_req | baseline_ppk | quant_savings | adjusted_ppk | cache_hit_rate | effective_ppk | price_per_1k | margin_per_1k
Sample data rows (illustrative):
us-west1 | rwd-13b | fp16 | 64 | 250 | 340 | 0.0095 | 0.12 | =baseline_ppk*(1-quant_savings) | 0.15 | =adjusted_ppk*(1-cache_hit_rate) | 0.020 | =price_per_1k-effective_ppk
us-east1 | rwd-70b | int8 | 128 | 40 | 600 | 0.032 | 0.18 | =baseline_ppk*(1-quant_savings) | 0.06 | =adjusted_ppk*(1-cache_hit_rate) | 0.050 | =price_per_1k-effective_ppk

Cache Prioritization tab (methodology):
- Priority score = (tokens_per_req * reqs_per_min) * latency_weight / regional_cost_index. Higher score = good candidate for prefix/KV caching.
- Template classification:
  * Static templates (billing receipts, legal notices) -> long TTL, high cache benefit.
  * Semi-static (support replies, onboarding flows) -> medium TTL, moderate benefit.
  * Dynamic conversational -> short TTL, low per-instance cache benefit but still useful for prefix reuse.
- TTL strategy recommendations: 5-15 minutes for interactive chat sessions; 4-24 hours for static triggers depending on update cadence.
- Memory vs savings tradeoff table (example):
  memory_cost_per_gb_per_day | expected_token_savings_per_day | net_savings
  0.55 | 1.2M tokens | +$0.66/day
  0.55 | 4.5M tokens | +$2.48/day

Runway Scenarios (projected 6 month snapshots):
- Scenario A (Conservative): No quantization changes; cache adoption grows from 2% -> 5%; throughput improvements minimal. Result: margin compresses by ~3 percentage points over 6 months under 10% monthly usage growth.
- Scenario B (Pragmatic optimize): Roll int8 for rwd-13b and rwd-70b in non-EU regions; targeted prefix cache for top-20 routes; introduce small batching tweaks. Metrics: cache adoption 25%, effective_ppk down by 18% on targeted SKUs; margin +6 pts; breakeven for implementation cost ~9 months.
- Scenario C (Aggressive): Aggressive quantization (4-bit) on rwd-13b in dedicated pools, global cache adoption 40%, and aggressive batching. Upside: margin +12 pts. Risks: quality regressions, higher engineering and validation cost, regional compliance gating for EU.

Key spreadsheet formulas (human-readable):
- tokens_per_min = reqs_per_min * tokens_per_req
- baseline_cost_per_min = tokens_per_min * baseline_ppk / 1000
- adjusted_ppk = baseline_ppk * (1 - quant_savings)  (quant_savings cell per model/quant profile)
- effective_ppk = adjusted_ppk * (1 - cache_hit_rate)
- margin_per_1k = price_per_1k - effective_ppk
- priority_score = tokens_per_min * latency_weight / regional_cost_index

Operational notes and rollout pattern:
- Canary plan: deploy quantized kernels to us-west1 (low-risk), monitor quality via eval harness (automated A/B sampling of customer routes), then proceed to us-east1 and finally eu-west1 after legal check.
- Console changes: expose per-route effective_ppk and cache hit rate metrics; add alert when effective_ppk crosses SLA tier thresholds.
- Billing: map SKU tags to billing pipeline to ensure customers see consistent pricing; ensure reserved capacity discounts apply post-smoothing.
- SRE: set guardrails for node memory per cache region; autoscaling policies must account for additional memory footprint for long TTL caches.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a per-route sequence-length histogram (Linear OPT-1021) to better size batching buckets.
- Bench: validate 4-bit inference kernel latency/throughput at target seq lengths (infra ticket INF-589).
- Compliance: confirm whether routing EU requests to non-EU regions is acceptable for latency-tiered customers.
- Customer comms: plan for explicit opt-in or notification if model variant/quantization may change output slightly.

Recommendations (short list):
1) 8-week pilot: int8 for rwd-13b in us-west1 + prefix cache for top-25 templates (owner: Priya).
2) Build a "cache-cost" daily job (owner: Oscar) to reconcile memory delta vs token savings by region.
3) Add margin guardrails and dashboard in Console (owner: Lena) to alert when effective_ppk > threshold for specific SLA tiers.
4) Implement per-route quantization opt-in & A/B evals to detect quality regressions before wide rollout.

Next steps & owners:
- Priya Natarajan: coordinate pilot, finalize target SKUs for Q4 backlog.
- Ethan Morales (Eng infra): run kernel benches and provide perf numbers for int8/4-bit (target date: 2024-10-18).
- Oscar Ruiz (SRE): advise on cache memory limits and daily job requirements.
- Lena Kim (Product): wire Console dashboards and alerting.

Notes to self: this is a working workbook with conservative default coefficients. Update with real per-route telemetry before finalizing confluence write-up.
